title: tenant-graceful-shepherd-and-circuit-unplug-hotfix
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilizes tenant graceful unplug flow and prevents spurious regional circuit tripping under short maintenance windows. Backported to v2026.02-release.
description: Motivation: production incidents in the past 48 hours revealed two correlated failure modes during tenant unplug (customer-initiated detach and scheduled maintenance): 1) abrupt KV cache eviction left in-flight requests failing with 503s; 2) regional circuit state machines could flip to OPEN due to transient health probe flaps and then remain sticky, causing cascading regional failover and load oscillation. This PR provides a minimal, low-risk hotfix that introduces a ’graceful shepherd’ flow for tenant unplug and hardens the circuit state transition logic to tolerate transient probe failures. Summary of changes: - Introduces a tenant-unplug coordinator that drains inflight shared KV cache sessions and transitions tenant routing into a ’soft-standby’ window (configurable ttl) before full detach. This avoids dropping requests and allows in-progress batches to complete. - Adds a transient-probe debounce layer and bounded reopen backoff to the regional circuit breaker so a sequence of short probe failures does not permanently open circuits. - Adds explicit telemetry and audit events for unplug start/finish and for circuit soft-deny transitions to aid post-incident analysis. Rollout strategy: - Deploy as a hotfix to main, then staggered rollout to release branches: v2026.02-release and v2025.12-legacy. - Feature gate for graceful-shepherd enabled by default for dedicated and private customers; can be toggled per-customer via tenant flags for additional vetting. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for coordinator state transitions (drain -> soft-standby -> detached) and for circuit debounce paths. - Integration test harness simulating concurrent request streams during unplug; validated no 5xx spike in local perf lab. - Canary deployment to a subset of regions (us-west-2 then eu-west-1) with streaming telemetry checks and automatic rollback on error-rate delta > +1.5% over baseline. Backport and urgency: This is a hotfix tied to customer-impacting incidents (SUP-4312). Targeted for immediate merge and backport. Risk: Low-medium. Changes are conservative, mostly additive control logic and feature-guarded. KV drain uses existing eviction APIs and respects current SLO prioritization. Notes: This PR is intentionally small and focused to minimize blast radius; follow-up PRs will (a) add a formal visibility page in Console and (b) provide an admin tool to trigger manual shepherd windows. References: Linear ENG-1952, incident notes SUP-4312.
